nodes.norm_label: no lookup ever raises out of the nightly job
nodes.rationale: base.run and lookups.run turn every failure into an unreadable result naming the exception class; the hr_nightly step catches anything else and prints 'registrations: failed' so the command never fails and the next night retries.

nodes.label: Nightly registrations step (hr_nightly)
nodes.rationale: Syncs each body's verified flag from its adapter's fixtures, then runs tonight's lookups and prints a 'registrations:' line; never raises out of the command. Execution moved it before the digest so that night's findings are in that morning's email.

nodes.label: No PII in register logs
nodes.rationale: Logs carry only the error class, the body code and the registration pk, never the number, the name or the page; unexpected exceptions are recorded by class name because their message may carry the number or a name.

nodes.label: Registration number formats and normalisation
nodes.rationale: GMC and GPhC are seven digits; NMC is two digits, a letter, four digits, a letter (12A3456B, correcting the spec's example AB12C3456). Whitespace is stripped and letters upper-cased before the format check, on the form and in the service, so a typed form such as '12a 3456 b' never reaches a register.

nodes.label: Pause a body after three unreadable lookups
nodes.norm_label: pause a body after three unreadable lookups
nodes.rationale: PAUSE_AFTER = 3 unreadable results in a row across a body sets paused_at and the schedule skips it (a body that pauses mid-run is skipped from then on). HR's Unpause or a successful on-demand lookup lifts it so the schedule resumes the same night; after an Unpause the earlier unreadable lookups still count, so HR runs Check now once.

nodes.label: Registration alerts in the morning digest
nodes.norm_label: registration alerts in the morning digest

nodes.label: Fixture sidecar files (.surname, .number)
nodes.rationale: The surname sidecar makes the name check part of the test; the number sidecar is for parsers like the Welsh list that pick their row by number.

nodes.label: Welsh performers list row layout (mpl_wales)
nodes.rationale: Has no LABELS, RESTRICTION_LABELS or NAME_MARKER: it finds the row by number and expects number, name and status on consecutive lines.

nodes.label: Status read only from labelled fields; unknown wording is unreadable
nodes.norm_label: status read only from labelled fields; unknown wording is unreadable
nodes.rationale: A status is the value after a label such as 'Registration status'; problem words are checked before clear words, as whole words, and a value with 'not' or 'without' is never clear. A status is clear only when its trimmed value equals a known clear phrase; a problem stem (suspen, restrict, condition, lapse, eras ...) is a problem; anything else is unreadable so an unknown wording is never good news. Labelled restriction fields turn a clear status into a problem; not-found wording is consulted only when no status field is on the page.

nodes.label: Problem vocabulary checked before clear
nodes.rationale: 'Registered without a licence to practise' contains a problem phrase, so checking problem words before clear words is what prevents a false clear; the order must be kept.

nodes.label: Fixture consent and personal data rule
nodes.norm_label: fixture consent and personal data rule
nodes.rationale: Pages hold a real, publicly registered name and number and nothing else personal; never capture a page for anyone who has not agreed.

nodes.label: Register status classification (exact CLEAR, whole-word PROBLEM, PROBLEM_STEMS, else unreadable)
nodes.norm_label: register status classification (exact clear, whole-word problem, problem_stems, else unreadable)
nodes.rationale: A value is clear only when, ignoring case, spaces and punctuation, it is exactly a CLEAR value, so 'Registered - suspension pending' is not clear; a problem matches the body's wordings or shared stems; anything else is unreadable. GMC's GP Register field is read against GP_REGISTER_CLEAR the same way.

nodes.label: account.html (Account page)
nodes.rationale: Shows the signed-in email, a change-password link and a passkeys table with per-passkey Remove. Passkeys sit alongside the password ('your password still works'). Adding one asks for the password too when needs_password is set: 'a check that it's you, not someone at a computer you left signed in'. The Add button is hidden until JavaScript reveals it; a noscript note explains it needs JavaScript.

nodes.label: passkey_added_email.txt (Passkey added notice)
nodes.rationale: Security notification after a passkey is added: if it wasn't you, someone else has been signed in as you, so reset the password ticking 'Also remove all my passkeys', then tell an HR admin; links to the Account page listing passkeys.

nodes.label: Passkey nudge banner
nodes.rationale: Offered once per browser, by the script, where no passkey has been used, and only in the minutes after signing in: the one time adding a passkey needs no password (accounts/recent_auth.py).

nodes.label: base.html (Site base layout)
nodes.rationale: Two theme-color metas (the --accent light and dark values) rather than a manifest's single theme_color.

nodes.label: div.html (Site form layout)

nodes.label: field.html (Design-system field markup)
nodes.rationale: One field in the design system's markup (components.css), shared by form.as_div and field.as_field_group: label (no colon), control, help, then each error as an alert. nodes.label: people/_documents.html (My record Documents card)
nodes.rationale: The person's own files that are not HR-only and not superseded, newest first; every link goes through the audited documents:download view rather than a direct media URL.

nodes.label: people/me.html (My record page)
nodes.rationale: Shows employment facts (start, continuous service, position, contracted units), the AM/PM working pattern grid, the onboarding checklist, then the Registrations, Checks, Training and Documents cards, and an editable personal-details form; a polite notice when no employee record is linked to the login.

nodes.label: locked_out.html (Too many attempts page)
nodes.rationale: Rendered by accounts/lockout.py with status 429 when a password sign-in is refused (too many failures for this account, or against too many accounts from this address). nodes.label: login.html (Log in page)
nodes.rationale: Password form plus a 'Sign in with a passkey' button hidden until passkeys.js arms it; links to the forgotten-password flow.

nodes.label: password_reset_confirm.html (Set password from link page)
nodes.rationale: One template serves both the invitation ('Welcome, choose a password') and the reset, switched on is_invitation; setting the password signs the person straight in. An invalid or used link offers to request another or ask an HR admin.

nodes.label: password_reset_done.html (Check your email page)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately non-committal ('If there's a login for that address') so the page does not reveal which emails have accounts; the link works for seven days.

nodes.label: training/session.html (Record a training session page)
nodes.rationale: Records a face-to-face group session once via sessions.record_session. Back goes to the admin session list for HR or to My team for a manager.

nodes.label: password_reset_email.txt (Password reset email body)
nodes.rationale: Single-use reset link with expiry; 'If that wasn't you, ignore this, your password stays as it is.'

nodes.label: password_reset_subject.txt (Password reset email subject)
nodes.rationale: Subject line 'Reset your Practice HR password'.

nodes.rationale: When a register body's parser is not yet verified against a saved page, check-now records only the Lookup, not a check, and warns the user to read the result with care - an unproven scraper cannot write compliance evidence.

nodes.norm_label: seeded absence types (al, bh, study, toil, sick, mat, pat, spl, adopt, comp, dep, unpaid, other)

nodes.label: AbsenceType flags drive the workflow
nodes.rationale: Types are configurable rows; paid, uses_pot, needs_approval, self_certified, calendar_label, payroll_reportable and health_sensitive decide behaviour instead of code testing a type's name.

nodes.label: Accrual integral (entitlement as a day-by-day sum over the leave year)
nodes.norm_label: accrual integral (entitlement as a day-by-day sum over the leave year)
nodes.rationale: Each active day accrues (weeks + tier extra) x contracted weekly amount / days in year, so mid-year starters and leavers, tier steps, fixed-term and concurrent contracts pro-rate naturally and a leap year accrues the same as a common year. Pure: reads people rows and policies, writes nothing.

nodes.label: Automatic bank-holiday absences
nodes.rationale: Approved auto rows are created only for bank holidays the person works under the two pot handlings and cancelled with a cancellation line when the pattern or policy stops implying them; idempotent.

nodes.label: Bank-holiday pot formula (year's bank holidays / 5 as weeks)
nodes.norm_label: bank-holiday pot formula (year's bank holidays / 5 as weeks)
nodes.rationale: Under pro-rata pot handling the number of bank holidays in the year divided by five is used as the weeks figure in the accrual integral.

nodes.label: C2 ruling: bank holidays charged only by automatic rows
nodes.norm_label: c2 ruling: bank holidays charged only by automatic rows
nodes.rationale: From the final review: ordinary range bookings skip bank holidays under every handling, overlap checks compare ordinary with ordinary and automatic with automatic, and kept automatic rows are re-costed; the spec was amended in section 4.

nodes.label: Costing a booking from the working pattern
nodes.norm_label: costing a booking from the working pattern
nodes.rationale: Cost is the sum of AM/PM units from the pattern in force each day, skipping closed days and bank holidays under closed handling; a weekend or a day with no pattern costs zero rather than erroring.

nodes.label: sync_entitlement writes the difference as one revision line
nodes.norm_label: sync_entitlement writes the difference as one revision line
nodes.rationale: Reconciles entitlement lines with accrual.entitlement by writing only the delta with a cause note; idempotent, so a second sync or a change that rounds to nothing writes nothing.

nodes.label: I1 ruling: pots open synced and the nightly bootstraps them
nodes.norm_label: i1 ruling: pots open synced and the nightly bootstraps them
nodes.rationale: pots.for_day writes the entitlement (and an AL pot's automatic bank holidays) on creation and the nightly opens current-year pots for every active employment; because for_day now writes, plan 3 must not call it on a GET.

nodes.label: MIDDAY partial-day cap (13:00)
nodes.rationale: A partial day is capped at the units of the halves it touches, split at 13:00, so hours booked cannot exceed what the pattern says the person works.

nodes.label: Missing policy is a ValidationError naming it, never a silent zero
nodes.norm_label: missing policy is a validationerror naming it, never a silent zero
nodes.rationale: A pot-backed type with no policy for the contract type must fail loudly with the policy named, so a misconfiguration never shows as zero entitlement.

nodes.label: Nightly safety net (nightly.run re-syncs every open pot and bank holidays)
nodes.norm_label: nightly safety net (nightly.run re-syncs every open pot and bank holidays)
nodes.rationale: Repeats the signal-driven re-sync for every open pot each night so a missed signal cannot leave an entitlement stale; hooked into hr_nightly.

nodes.label: Overlapping requested or approved absences refused in the service
nodes.norm_label: overlapping requested or approved absences refused in the service

nodes.label: Re-costing an approved absence as an adjustment line
nodes.norm_label: re-costing an approved absence as an adjustment line
nodes.rationale: After a pattern change an HR admin re-prices an approved absence; the difference is written as an ADJUSTMENT line rather than editing the booking line.

nodes.label: Sickness self-certified when shorter than seven days
nodes.norm_label: sickness self-certified when shorter than seven days
nodes.rationale: SICK needs no approval and no pot; it is recorded approved and flagged self-certified when under SELF_CERT_DAYS (7).

nodes.label: Step rounding (0.25 hour, 0.5 session, half up)
nodes.norm_label: step rounding (0.25 hour, 0.5 session, half up)
nodes.rationale: Units are two-place Decimals rounded to the policy step, half up, so entitlements and costs land on bookable amounts.

nodes.label: API absences window uses overlap, not containment
nodes.norm_label: api absences window uses overlap, not containment
nodes.rationale: An absence starting before 'from' and ending after 'to' must be returned; containment was the Breathe bug recorded in the rota's spec.

nodes.label: Calendar shows calendar_label only; sickness category never rendered
nodes.norm_label: calendar shows calendar_label only; sickness category never rendered
nodes.rationale: Colleagues see Leave/Sick/Away; a health category appears only on the employee's own page, their manager's view and the admin.

nodes.label: email/compliance_digest.txt (Compliance digest email)
nodes.rationale: Lines regrouped by person, each with the item label, when it is due and its link; the recipient is reminded again while items are outstanding.

nodes.label: Digest groups paused-body items under 'The registers'
nodes.norm_label: digest groups paused-body items under 'the registers'
nodes.rationale: A paused body's DueItem has employee=None, so the digest's sort key and the template's regroup (by 'who' instead of item.employee) tolerate it; registration lines read 'found <date>' or 'not recorded'.

nodes.label: Automatic bank-holiday absence row
nodes.rationale: Bank holidays are charged automatically as approved absence rows made by the nightly job. Once such a row is cancelled it stays cancelled and the nightly does not recreate it (so an admin's cancellation is not silently undone). To charge the day later, Charge again makes a new automatic row and approves it, only if the person's working pattern and policy still charge that day; the old row stays cancelled for history.

nodes.label: Cancellation line returns cost to pot
nodes.norm_label: cancellation line returns cost to pot
nodes.rationale: Cancelling an approved absence does not delete its charge: the cost goes back to its pot with a separate cancellation ledger line, recorded as the acting user.

nodes.label: Keeping-in-touch (KIT) days
nodes.rationale: KIT days are recorded against an existing absence from My absences, with the date constrained to that absence's start and end dates, and listed under it.

nodes.label: Check-and-confirm leave preview
nodes.rationale: Submitting the form first previews the cost, remaining balance, balance after and other waiting requests; confirming re-posts the same fields as hidden inputs with confirm=1, so nothing is booked until the person has seen what it costs.

nodes.label: Over-balance warning (soft limit)
nodes.rationale: Asking for more than the balance is allowed, not blocked: the requester can still ask and the approver sees it flagged; a manager recording it can still record it. The warning appears on the preview, the decide page and the My absences row.

nodes.label: Progressive-enhancement request field groups
nodes.rationale: Fields are grouped by purpose (what and when, part of a day, sickness, family leave). Every group shows without script; absence/request.js hides and disables the groups the chosen absence type does not use, from flags on the type's option. Part of a day is offered whenever the allowance is in hours, for every type.

nodes.label: Import cycles through the deferred import in employments._cancel_after
nodes.norm_label: import cycles through the deferred import in employments._cancel_after
nodes.rationale: All 19 import cycles run through one deferred import at people/services/employments.py:84-85, where _cancel_after imports absence bookings and bank_holidays to cancel a leaver's later absences, while absence services import people.services at module top (policies.py:7, bookings.py:11, bank_holidays.py:11).

nodes.label: registers/admin/unpause.html (Unpause register body confirm)
nodes.rationale: RegisterBodyAdmin.unpause confirm page in the admin: GET only shows it; the POST calls lookups.unpause so scheduled lookups run again tonight.

nodes.label: Register pause after three unreadable lookups (Unpause)
nodes.norm_label: register pause after three unreadable lookups (unpause)
nodes.rationale: A successful Check now lifts the pause by itself; after a manual Unpause the three old failures still count until a lookup succeeds, so one more failure re-pauses.

nodes.label: Register lookups auto-pause after three unreadable pages
nodes.norm_label: register lookups auto-pause after three unreadable pages
nodes.rationale: Scheduled lookups against a register stop after three in a row could not read its page (the site likely changed); a human explicitly unpauses so they run again that night.

nodes.label: documents/policies.html (My policies page)
nodes.rationale: Each policy that applies to the person with its current version, a status, the Read link (the audited download) and Sign until signed; a new version asks for a new signature.

nodes.label: documents/sign.html (Sign a policy page)
nodes.rationale: Signing asks for proof that it is the person: the password typed again or one of their own passkeys, so nobody else can sign for them at a computer left signed in.

nodes.rationale: The queue lists requests routed to the user's employee (all for HR admins); the decider is always recorded, an HR admin may decide anything, and an approver who is off that day can still decide.

nodes.label: The chase: requests waiting more than CHASE_AFTER_WORKING_DAYS, emailed once
nodes.norm_label: the chase: requests waiting more than chase_after_working_days, emailed once
nodes.rationale: Counts working days since the request and stamps chased_at so HR admins are emailed about each waiting request only once.

nodes.norm_label: a decider never decides their own request

nodes.norm_label: one email door that never raises (absence.mail.send)
nodes.rationale: A mail relay fault must not surface in a page: send returns False, logs the failure, and the dashboard shows it.

nodes.label: Min-present warning ('Approving leaves fewer than N present')
nodes.norm_label: min-present warning ('approving leaves fewer than n present')
nodes.rationale: The decide page warns when approving would leave a team below Team.min_present on any day of the request.

nodes.label: Negative balance carries in full at year end
nodes.norm_label: negative balance carries in full at year end
nodes.rationale: A negative balance is carried as a negative carry-in and shown as such, never silently zeroed.

nodes.label: Payroll changes report (eight sheets saved with a PayrollRun)
nodes.norm_label: payroll changes report (eight sheets saved with a payrollrun)
nodes.rationale: Monthly spreadsheet for the payroll bureau: starters, leavers, contract and pay changes, sickness, unpaid, family leave and TOIL; dates and units only, never a sickness category, never pay arithmetic.

nodes.label: TOIL lots carried as TOIL_EARNED lines with their earn date, never capped
nodes.norm_label: toil lots carried as toil_earned lines with their earn date, never capped
nodes.rationale: Year end was rewritten so each unused TOIL lot keeps its earn date and expires by toil_expires_after_days rather than being capped.

nodes.label: Year end: carry to the policy cap, expire the rest
nodes.norm_label: year end: carry to the policy cap, expire the rest
nodes.rationale: close() carries the balance up to carry_over_max_weeks x contracted amount and expires the remainder; idempotent via 'year end' notes, so running twice doubles nothing.

nodes.label: Presence headcount (N of M present)
nodes.rationale: Per working day the team calendar shows how many of the headcount are present, omitted on weekends and bank holidays, so approvers can judge cover; the decide page reuses the same per-day off/present data for the request's dates.

nodes.label: Leave-year pots open overnight
nodes.rationale: A balance pot may not exist yet for a leave year: this year's and next year's open overnight, and a later year's opens when leave in it is approved. Pages show 'Not opened yet' instead of failing; a missing contract or allowance policy is shown as a distinct error for an HR admin to check.

nodes.label: TOIL lifecycle (claim, approve, take, expire)
nodes.rationale: TOIL is claimed for time already worked beyond normal hours; the approver decides it; approval adds the units to the person's TOIL dated the day worked; it is taken by requesting leave of type TOIL; it can be used for a set number of days after the day worked, so earned lots carry use-by deadlines and expire.

nodes.label: Already-decided guard on decision pages
nodes.rationale: When a leave request or TOIL claim is already decided or cancelled, the decision page shows what happened, by whom and when (with any comment) instead of the approve/decline form, so the same item cannot be decided twice from an old link.

nodes.label: Record leave or TOIL on someone's behalf
nodes.norm_label: record leave or toil on someone's behalf
nodes.rationale: A line manager (for their reports) or an HR admin (for anyone) can record sickness on the day, leave agreed in person, or TOIL already worked. It is approved at once and the employee is emailed, bypassing the request/approve round trip.

nodes.rationale: The per-app role carries admin only; access to an app is any active HR login. An access flag can be added later if wanted.

nodes.norm_label: accounts app (moved from the rota: login, invitations, passkeys, axes lockout)

nodes.norm_label: openid connect provider (django-oauth-toolkit, code flow, sub/email/employee_id claims)

nodes.norm_label: rota (gp rota app, oidc relying party)

nodes.norm_label: rota change: sign in with the practice account
nodes.rationale: The only rota change in this release; the rota password form stays only for the superuser and rota passkeys are retired once every account has signed in through HR.

nodes.label: Shared Django default password hashers
nodes.rationale: Neither repository sets PASSWORD_HASHERS, so a hash string moves between them unchanged.

nodes.label: HR system as the identity provider
nodes.norm_label: hr system as the identity provider
nodes.rationale: GPs will not accept two logins; HR holds every employee anyway and the passkey, invitation and lockout work already exists in accounts, so no shared package is needed.

nodes.label: Separate Django project in its own repository
nodes.norm_label: separate django project in its own repository
nodes.rationale: The rota models GPs only and holds almost no personal data; an HR system covers every employee and holds health, DBS and bank data. Putting it in the rota would invert the population and undo the decision that the rota holds no leave balances.

nodes.label: SQLite WAL and a filesystem document store
nodes.norm_label: sqlite wal and a filesystem document store
nodes.rationale: At one practice's headcount it is plenty and the backup tooling exists; Postgres only if concurrency ever shows.

nodes.label: Signing with re-authentication (password or passkey)
nodes.rationale: A signature should prove presence, not just a session; a wrong password counts towards the lockout.
